content.value: IN FLIGHT NOW: SURVEYING (opened at STRATEGIZE 2026-07-14). The co-located site deploy is PROVEN PERFECT for manual/CLI trigger — W4 walked all 6 stages (PLAN→BUILD→STAGE→HEALTH→SWITCH→RETIRE) to a live URL serving REAL content on guerrilla, force-nonce mints distinct build_ids, rollback in 0.21s, zero external accounts. This wave closes the LAST original 'perfect deploy' gap: PUBLISH-TO-LIVE AUTO-UPDATE. Edit in Studio, hit publish, the bound co-located site re-deploys itself — no manual bp cloud site deploy. This Paper is the wave's living story; every phase appends. Digest appends the survey digest + verify plan; Decide appends decisions + the wave plan; Review closes it.

When a user PUBLISHES content in their Barkpark (a document mutation on the site's bound workspace/project/dataset), the co-located site AUTOMATICALLY re-deploys — walking the same 6-stage state machine to a fresh live build carrying the new content — with NO manual trigger. Reuse the existing webhook-realtime/revalidation machinery and the content-mutation PubSub broadcasts (documents:ws:<wsid>:<dataset>) — do NOT invent a new event bus. The deploy trigger already exists (POST /v1/sites/:id/deploy on the control plane); this wave WIRES a content-publish event to that trigger for every site bound to the mutated dataset.

MUST be: DEBOUNCED/COALESCED (a burst of publishes = ONE rebuild, not N — a rebuild is ~10s of npm); FAIL-CLOSED (a broken content state must still die at HEALTH and never reach visitors — the existing gate already does this); IDEMPOTENT (the force-nonce path gives each auto-rebuild a fresh build_id); OBSERVABLE (the deployment stream shows it was content-triggered, not manual). Keep STANDALONE-FIRST: works with the box's own content + webhooks, zero external accounts. DELIVER: the publish→deploy binding (which sites listen to which dataset), the debounce/coalesce, an auto-vs-manual trigger-provenance field on the deployment, then a LIVE proof on guerrilla — publish a NEW paper, watch the bound site auto-rebuild to a live URL whose bp-content-rev/bp-doc-id reflect the new content, within a bounded time.

The deployment stream shows an entry labelled 'content publish' not 'manual'. Ten rapid publishes produce ONE rebuild, not ten. A publish that breaks the build dies silently at HEALTH; the last-good build stays live. This is the Kinsta/Vercel 'git push → it just deploys' reflex, except the trigger is Publish and the transport is Barkpark's own content mutations — zero external accounts.

blocks.text: The architectural crux the survey must settle

content.value: The content publish fires on the CONTENT box (guerrilla): tap_broadcast/broadcast_document_mutation in api/lib/barkpark/content/broadcast.ex emits on documents:<dataset> and documents:ws:<wsid>:<dataset>, and the Webhooks.Dispatcher (api/lib/barkpark/webhooks/dispatcher.ex) already fires HMAC-signed HTTP off the same mutation on publish. But the site→dataset BINDING (sites.bootstrap_workspace/project/dataset) lives on the CONTROL PLANE (cloud/), and so does the deploy trigger (POST /v1/sites/:id/deploy → deploy.ex → box_relay.ex). PubSub is in-node (box only); it cannot cross to the CP. So the box must NOTIFY the CP of a relevant publish, OR the CP must learn the binding+debounce+trigger from a box-fired event.

MY LEAN (tentative): the CP OWNS the binding, debounce, and trigger — it already holds sites.bootstrap_dataset, the deploy queue (serialized, flock depth 1), and the deploy machinery. The box's only job is to NOTIFY 'dataset X had a publish'. The cleanest notify reuses the EXISTING Webhooks.Dispatcher (durable, HMAC-signed, retrying — the same transport as publish→revalidate): register ONE auto-deploy webhook endpoint (dataset-scoped) at site-create, pointing at a CP receiver; publish → Dispatcher → CP receiver resolves dataset→[bound sites], debounces per-site (Oban unique/scheduled window, mirroring the indx debounce pattern), and enqueues the EXISTING deploy with force=true and provenance=content-auto. Provenance = one new column on the CP deployments table (trigger source: manual|content-auto) surfaced in the stream.

TENSION TO RESOLVE: charter D12 seeded a lean toward a BOX-side Oban debounce lifecycle-hook (indx/edge_projector pattern), explicitly 'NOT webhook-to-self'. That was pre-cross-host thinking. Webhook-to-CP is NOT webhook-to-self — it is the revalidation shape the wish names. But the STANDALONE-FIRST clause ('the box's own content + webhooks') may argue for a box-local trigger path when the CP is co-located. The survey must settle: (a) box-notifies-CP-via-Dispatcher vs box-side-Oban-hook-that-calls-CP vs box-triggers-its-own-/v1/admin/site-deploy; (b) where the debounce lives; (c) whether standalone-first forces a CP-free path. I am NOT deciding this now — two explore rounds resolve it. Width is cheap; the survey casts wide.

PRIORITIES this wave, in order: (1) settle the crux (where binding+debounce+trigger live, and the notify transport) with EVIDENCE, not preference; (2) the publish→deploy binding + dataset→sites resolution; (3) debounce/coalesce (burst → one rebuild) reusing the indx/Oban pattern, no new bus; (4) trigger-provenance field + observable stream; (5) confirm fail-closed HEALTH + force-nonce idempotency inherit for free (do NOT rebuild them); (6) the LIVE proof on guerrilla — publish a NEW paper, bound site auto-rebuilds to a live URL whose bp-doc-id/bp-content-rev reflect it, within a bounded time. Reuse, don't invent: the Dispatcher, the PubSub topics, the 6-stage machine, the force-nonce, the HEALTH gate are all built and proven.

15 scouts reported. The crux is SETTLED by architecture, not preference. The site->dataset binding (sites.bootstrap_workspace/project/dataset) lives EXCLUSIVELY on the control plane (cloud/lib/barkpark_cloud/registry/site.ex); the content box (api/) has ZERO schema or code for it (grep of api/lib returns nothing). PubSub is in-node only. The ONLY existing off-box transport off a publish is Webhooks.Dispatcher (HMAC HTTP, durable, retrying, dedup on event_id). Therefore: the CP OWNS binding + dataset->sites resolution + debounce + trigger; the box only NOTIFIES. Unanimous across content-broadcast-seam, site-binding-location, cp-deploy-trigger, cross-host-config-map, standalone-co-located-mode.

REUSE SURFACE (established, do not re-litigate): (a) NOTIFY = register ONE dataset-scoped webhook row (events like publish/unpublish/delete) pointed at a NEW CP receiver URL, at site-create, via the EXISTING CP->box admin-token relay (Registry.relay_admin/4; wire_site_url/dwb-6 is live prior art for the CP registering a webhook row on a box). Box-side code = ZERO. This is NOT 'webhook-to-self' -- box (guerrilla) and CP (barkpark.cloud) are distinct public hosts, so SafeOutbound does not block it. (b) TRIGGER = Sites.Deploy.enqueue/3 + start/1 are plain in-process Elixir (no HTTP/PAT); a CP receiver (Oban worker or controller) calls them directly. GitHub-push handle_production_push is the existing precedent for a non-user, in-process, dedup'd deploy trigger. (c) FORCE-NONCE (D36) is REAL on origin/main: enqueue/3, build_id/4, maybe_force_nonce fold System.system_time() into the build_id hash. (d) FAIL-CLOSED HEALTH is inherited FOR FREE -- the gate lives in the bash script + box executor + CP normalize_state ('failure beats the lifecycle word'); settle_live fires only on :succeeded; pinned by sites_deploy_test.exs:169. Any auto-trigger that reuses enqueue/start inherits it. (e) PROVENANCE is greenfield and clean: deployment_json/1 is the SOLE base serializer, so one add of a deployments.trigger column (manual|content-auto) propagates to list/get/deploy-response; the environment enum is the exact precedent.

WHICH MUTATIONS FIRE A REBUILD = publish, unpublish, delete (3 of the 6 real events). NOT create/update/discardDraft: Writer coerces every ordinary write's status back to 'draft' (writer.ex:89-95, 452-458), so create/update never touch the published row; discardDraft deletes only the draft. 'patch' is subscribable in @valid_events but is NEVER emitted (resolves to 'update'). Canon-confirmed at webhook-realtime.md:42-44. Edge case: a delete of a never-published (draft-only) doc still fires 'delete' -> a harmless debounce-absorbed no-op rebuild.

DEBOUNCE prior art is real and proven 3x on main -- Indx IndexerWorker, EdgeProjector ProjectorWorker, GitHub MirrorJob -- all use Oban 'unique keys + schedule_in' to collapse a burst into one job. The CP runs its OWN mature Oban (8+ workers: stale_deployment_reaper, trial_expiry_worker, device_auth_reaper, ...). So a CP-side debounce keyed on site_id, schedule_in N, is buildable with a ready primitive -- NOT a copy of a cloud/ module (the 'indx/edge_projector' modules live in api/, not cloud/; the CP replicates the SHAPE).

content.value: Q1 DEBOUNCE HOME + double-debounce: D12/backlog task leaned box-side Oban (files: api/lib), but that predates the box/CP-split discovery -- a box-side debounce CANNOT resolve dataset->sites. Lean: ONE debounce, CP-side, keyed on site_id; box notify stays UNDEBOUNCED (Dispatcher already fires per-commit). Must not stack a box debounce AND a CP debounce (adds ~5-10s twice against the ~15s target). Q2 REGISTRATION ROUTE SCOPE: unscoped /v1/webhooks (reuses the site-deploy admin token but an unscoped row over-fires across workspaces sharing a dataset NAME) vs scoped route (precise, needs a workspace-role token the CP may not hold). Single-tenant guerrilla is unaffected. Q3 CP RECEIVER SHAPE: worker-token /v1/internal/* path vs per-site-secret path like the GitHub bridge; and the NET-NEW HMAC verifier must be byte-for-byte with dispatcher.ex verify_signature/4 (t=/v1= parse, +-300s freshness, delivery-id dedup) or it silently breaks or opens a forgery hole. Q4 force=true ALWAYS vs rely on content_rev: content_rev hashes a dataset snapshot, so a real publish already changes build_id without force -- force is belt-and-suspenders for the byte-identical-republish edge case. Decide should pin this rather than reflexively force every auto-trigger.

7 verifiers ran on origin/main (24467ba38). Trust proofs > facts > prose. The crux held; two digest framings were CORRECTED by run-output, and one design simplification (per-site receiver) drops the trickiest correctness trap the survey raised.

V1 oban-coalescing (RUN, DECISIVE): the prior-art unique clause reused VERBATIM would STRAND a mid-build publish. Proof: with states incl :executing, a publish landing while the ~10s build is :executing matches the existing job (state in states, within the 30s period off inserted_at) -> conflict -> NOTHING inserted; the build already snapshotted content at start, so the site silently serves STALE content — the exact failure the wish forbids. Fix PROVEN by a passing scratch test: drop :executing -> states [:available,:scheduled] -> a mid-build publish finds no conflict and mints exactly ONE trailing rebuild, while a burst before build still collapses to one :scheduled job. 'assert trailing==[]' for the prior-art clause and 'length(trailing)==1' for the fix both pass. cloud/ runs Oban 2.23.0 (supervised, maintenance queue) — 'cloud/ has no Oban' comments are STALE.

V2 provenance thread-through (RUN): deployment_json/1 IS the sole base serializer (site_deployment_json/3 + deployment_with_site_json/1 both pipe through it) — one add propagates to all 3 response shapes. BUT the CORRECTION: Go's json.Unmarshal silently DROPS unknown keys (no DisallowUnknownFields, no custom UnmarshalJSON) — environment/content_rev are already dropped today. So 'trigger' is real in Postgres + raw JSON yet INVISIBLE in every CLI surface unless threaded through client.go SiteDeployment + siteDeploymentMap/spawnSiteStatusMap + streamSiteDeploy. Go baseline green (build/vet/test 5/5).

V3 cp-inbound-receiver (REFUTED the fear): cloud/ ALREADY ships TWO inbound HMAC receivers — Stripe /v1/billing/webhook (unauth, HMAC is the auth, raw-body cached) and GitHub /v1/webhooks/github/:site_id. StripeGateway.check_signatures is BYTE-FOR-BYTE the Barkpark dispatcher scheme (material 'ts.body', :crypto.mac sha256 |> Base.encode16(:lower), t=/v1= grammar, 300s tolerance, secrets list). THE PARITY TRAP: the GitHub verifier is a DIFFERENT scheme (sha256=<hex> over raw body, no timestamp) — copying it would REJECT every valid delivery. Template = StripeGateway, NOT github. deploy_static_site already does enqueue+start in-process, no PAT — the receiver mirrors it.

V4 which-mutations (RUN, CONFIRMED): grep 'tap_broadcast(' api/lib = exactly 11 sites, ALL under content/; only lifecycle.ex carries 'publish'(:170)/'unpublish'(:283)/'delete'(:412). writer.ex/edges.ex/sheets.ex fire only create/update (draft-level). discardDraft touches only the draft. Trigger set = {publish, unpublish, delete}, nailed. github-bridge reuses Content.publish_document (same single call site) — no parallel broadcast path.

V5 registration-scope + resolver: (workspace,project,dataset) is NOT unique across the sites table (only unique idx is team_id+slug; barkpark_id index is non-unique) — a naive dataset->sites triple filter would cross-trigger a site on a different box sharing default slugs (production/main). relay_admin CAN reach the flat /v1/webhooks/:dataset admin route (same require_admin pipeline as site-deploy). DECIDE RESOLUTION: the per-site receiver (D45) sidesteps this ENTIRELY — site_id is the PK, so no resolver and no barkpark_id-scoping is needed.

V6 notify-leg (RUN on origin/main): the publish->webhook seam is ALREADY wired and TRANSACTION-DEFERRED — Content.tap_broadcast -> maybe_dispatch_webhook -> Dispatcher.dispatch_async, queued in the txn, flushed on commit, CLEARED on rollback. So a broken/rolled-back publish NEVER fires the trigger — fail-closed inherits at the NOTIFY leg too. force-nonce is REAL (enqueue/3 + maybe_force_nonce folds System.system_time); content_rev already varies on a real publish so force is belt-and-suspenders. sites_deploy_test 22-25/0 including force-nonce distinctness + HEALTH-fail-never-switches. SafeOutbound permits public->public (blocks only private/loopback/metadata). CORRECTION: verify_signature is arity /5 (not /4) and caller-less in api/ — cloud/ must PORT the verify (separate mix app).

V7 repo-freshness (RUN): local dff867f71 was 8 behind origin/main 24467ba38 — local deploy.ex had enqueue/2 (NO force); origin has enqueue/3 + force-nonce. Half the survey ran against stale code. provenance is greenfield end-to-end (schema, struct, every serializer, the newest content-binding migration). GATE for every builder: branch off origin/main. (Decide already rebased local main to origin/main and pushed the Wave-5 charter on top.)

D42 — CP OWNS binding + trigger; the box only NOTIFIES via the existing Webhooks.Dispatcher (zero new box-side code). Why: PubSub is in-node; the Dispatcher is the only off-box transport off a publish; the binding lives only on the CP. Resolves D12's 'NOT webhook-to-self' — box and CP are distinct public hosts.
D43 — Trigger set = {publish, unpublish, delete}. Why: only these touch the published row (V4); create/update/discardDraft never change what a visitor sees; patch never emits.

D44 — ONE CP-side Oban debounce, unique on site_id, states [:available,:scheduled] — DROP :executing. content.value: The content publish fires on the CONTENT box (guerrilla): tap_broadcast/broadcast_document_mutation in api/lib/barkpark/content/broadcast.ex emits on documents:<dataset> and documents:ws:<wsid>:<dataset>, and the Webhooks.Dispatcher (api/lib/barkpark/webhooks/dispatcher.ex) already fires HMAC-signed HTTP off the same mutation on publish. PubSub is in-node (box only); it cannot cross to the CP. So the box must NOTIFY the CP of a relevant publish, OR the CP must learn the binding+debounce+trigger from a box-fired event.

The box's only job is to NOTIFY 'dataset X had a publish'. 7 verifiers ran on origin/main (24467ba38). Trust proofs > facts > prose. The crux held; two digest framings were CORRECTED by run-output, and one design simplification (per-site receiver) drops the trickiest correctness trap the survey raised.

V1 oban-coalescing (RUN, DECISIVE): the prior-art unique clause reused VERBATIM would STRAND a mid-build publish. Proof: with states incl :executing, a publish landing while the ~10s build is :executing matches the existing job (state in states, within the 30s period off inserted_at) -> conflict -> NOTHING inserted; the build already snapshotted content at start, so the site silently serves STALE content — the exact failure the wish forbids. Fix PROVEN by a passing scratch test: drop :executing -> states [:available,:scheduled] -> a mid-build publish finds no conflict and mints exactly ONE trailing rebuild, while a burst before build still collapses to one :scheduled job. 'assert trailing==[]' for the prior-art clause and 'length(trailing)==1' for the fix both pass. cloud/ runs Oban 2.23.0 (supervised, maintenance queue) — 'cloud/ has no Oban' comments are STALE.

V2 provenance thread-through (RUN): deployment_json/1 IS the sole base serializer (site_deployment_json/3 + deployment_with_site_json/1 both pipe through it) — one add propagates to all 3 response shapes. BUT the CORRECTION: Go's json.Unmarshal silently DROPS unknown keys (no DisallowUnknownFields, no custom UnmarshalJSON) — environment/content_rev are already dropped today. So 'trigger' is real in Postgres + raw JSON yet INVISIBLE in every CLI surface unless threaded through client.go SiteDeployment + siteDeploymentMap/spawnSiteStatusMap + streamSiteDeploy. Go baseline green (build/vet/test 5/5).

V3 cp-inbound-receiver (REFUTED the fear): cloud/ ALREADY ships TWO inbound HMAC receivers — Stripe /v1/billing/webhook (unauth, HMAC is the auth, raw-body cached) and GitHub /v1/webhooks/github/:site_id. StripeGateway.check_signatures is BYTE-FOR-BYTE the Barkpark dispatcher scheme (material 'ts.body', :crypto.mac sha256 |> Base.encode16(:lower), t=/v1= grammar, 300s tolerance, secrets list). THE PARITY TRAP: the GitHub verifier is a DIFFERENT scheme (sha256=<hex> over raw body, no timestamp) — copying it would REJECT every valid delivery. Template = StripeGateway, NOT github. deploy_static_site already does enqueue+start in-process, no PAT — the receiver mirrors it.

V4 which-mutations (RUN, CONFIRMED): grep 'tap_broadcast(' api/lib = exactly 11 sites, ALL under content/; only lifecycle.ex carries 'publish'(:170)/'unpublish'(:283)/'delete'(:412). writer.ex/edges.ex/sheets.ex fire only create/update (draft-level). discardDraft touches only the draft. Trigger set = {publish, unpublish, delete}, nailed. github-bridge reuses Content.publish_document (same single call site) — no parallel broadcast path.

V5 registration-scope + resolver: (workspace,project,dataset) is NOT unique across the sites table (only unique idx is team_id+slug; barkpark_id index is non-unique) — a naive dataset->sites triple filter would cross-trigger a site on a different box sharing default slugs (production/main). relay_admin CAN reach the flat /v1/webhooks/:dataset admin route (same require_admin pipeline as site-deploy). DECIDE RESOLUTION: the per-site receiver (D45) sidesteps this ENTIRELY — site_id is the PK, so no resolver and no barkpark_id-scoping is needed.

V6 notify-leg (RUN on origin/main): the publish->webhook seam is ALREADY wired and TRANSACTION-DEFERRED — Content.tap_broadcast -> maybe_dispatch_webhook -> Dispatcher.dispatch_async, queued in the txn, flushed on commit, CLEARED on rollback. So a broken/rolled-back publish NEVER fires the trigger — fail-closed inherits at the NOTIFY leg too. force-nonce is REAL (enqueue/3 + maybe_force_nonce folds System.system_time); content_rev already varies on a real publish so force is belt-and-suspenders. sites_deploy_test 22-25/0 including force-nonce distinctness + HEALTH-fail-never-switches. SafeOutbound permits public->public (blocks only private/loopback/metadata). CORRECTION: verify_signature is arity /5 (not /4) and caller-less in api/ — cloud/ must PORT the verify (separate mix app).

V7 repo-freshness (RUN): local dff867f71 was 8 behind origin/main 24467ba38 — local deploy.ex had enqueue/2 (NO force); origin has enqueue/3 + force-nonce. Half the survey ran against stale code. provenance is greenfield end-to-end (schema, struct, every serializer, the newest content-binding migration). GATE for every builder: branch off origin/main. (Decide already rebased local main to origin/main and pushed the Wave-5 charter on top.)

D42 — CP OWNS binding + trigger; the box only NOTIFIES via the existing Webhooks.Dispatcher (zero new box-side code). Why: PubSub is in-node; the Dispatcher is the only off-box transport off a publish; the binding lives only on the CP. Resolves D12's 'NOT webhook-to-self' — box and CP are distinct public hosts.
D43 — Trigger set = {publish, unpublish, delete}. Why: only these touch the published row (V4); create/update/discardDraft never change what a visitor sees; patch never emits.

D44 — ONE CP-side Oban debounce, unique on site_id, states [:available,:scheduled] — DROP :executing. Why (V1, RUN): :executing swallows a mid-build publish and serves stale content; dropping it collapses bursts AND mints exactly one trailing rebuild after the current build. Box notify stays undebounced (no double-debounce).

D45 — The receiver is PER-SITE: POST /v1/sites/webhooks/content-publish/:site_id (mirrors /v1/webhooks/github/:site_id). Why: eliminates the dataset->sites resolver AND the barkpark_id-scoping trap (V5) — site_id is the PK; the box already fans one delivery per registered webhook row.

D46 — HMAC verifier mirrors StripeGateway.check_signatures (material 'ts.body', t=/v1=, 300s, secrets list), NOT the GitHub verifier (V3 parity trap). Why: the box signs the Barkpark dispatcher scheme; the github sha256= scheme would reject every delivery. Ported into a small cloud/ module (cloud/ can't call api's caller-less verify).

D47 — Per-site secret sites.content_webhook_secret_encrypted (Vault-encrypted, mirroring github_webhook_secret_encrypted). Why: the CP must hold the secret to verify inbound; Webhook.changeset casts :secret on CREATE (exposed once), so the CP mints it, passes it in the box create call, stores the ciphertext.

Why: force guarantees a fresh build_id on byte-identical republish and is safe post-debounce (force is the opposite of a dedup key; the site_id-unique job prevents the race). Fail-closed HEALTH + force-nonce inherit free (V6).

D49 — Provenance = one deployments.trigger column (manual|content-auto, default manual), mirroring the environment enum, threaded through deployment_json/1 AND the Go CLI (V2 — Go silently drops unknown keys, so the CLI surface is required, not free).
